_comment: English-only production policy for @metacognition.hq — Metacognition for the AI age. How humans think, learn, build, and make decisions with technology.

page.brand_positioning: Metacognition for the AI age. How humans think, learn, build, and make decisions with technology.

generation.quota_behavior: 429 honors Retry-After (max 2 short retries), 401/403 no retry, 5xx/timeout limited retry, then static-fallback; no cost, no pipeline stop if fallback valid

content_strategy.note: Ratios controlled in rolling window 10-20 posts, not weekly exact

pillars.AI_JUDGMENT: AI and human judgment — automation bias, confidence calibration, hallucination
pillars.CODING: Coding and debugging — metacognition in debugging, tutorial hell, deskilling
pillars.LEARNING_TECH: Learning technical skills — learning to code with AI, cognitive offloading
pillars.PRODUCT: Product and startup decisions — planning fallacy in estimation, Goodhart's law, sunk cost in architecture
pillars.ATTENTION: Attention and digital behavior — context switching, notifications, focus
pillars.HUMAN_AI: Human-AI collaboration — when AI improves vs replaces thinking

allowed_topics: tutorial hell and illusion of competence
banned_topics: pure tech news without metacognitive lesson
weak or artificial link to metacognition
technology_examples: tutorial hell and illusion of competence

tone.style: informal, conversational, natural spoken English; second person; short sentences; strong hook in 3 seconds

pre_render._comment: Deterministic PRE-RENDER script gate (producer + pipeline) params only. QA thresholds are UNCHANGED: narration 150-260 words and rendered video 60-120 seconds stay the final authority. word_target is prompt/revision guidance to keep a safe duration margin, never a gate.

english.style: karaoke word-by-word, max 2-3 short lines, big font, high contrast, inside safe zone, above caption and IG buttons

layout.note: FA layer removed, space used for bigger diagram, code visual, evidence card, confidence meter, decision tree, prediction graph, human-AI network

visual.style: network / node-edge diagrams, gold on dark marble, animated, episode-aware, technology-relevant
rules: nodes and edges must come from the episode (no reel-01 leftovers)
every scene animates; no static picture longer than 4 seconds
diagram never covers subtitles; subtitles never leave safe zone
logo is procedural stand-in until official file exists
visual must be relevant to technology angle: code-like, confidence meter, decision tree, prediction-vs-result, human-AI network

palette_qa._comment: Rendered-palette QA for the warm profile palette (matte black / charcoal / gold / amber / bronze / ivory). Blue, navy, cyan and purple stay prohibited: a decoded frame must not show a meaningful cold region. ONE configuration shared by the pre-encode plan gate, the final decoded-frame visual_semantics check and the tests (build/palette_qa.py). Key semantics: Three prohibited cold families are classified INDEPENDENTLY: blue/navy (blue_min_excess = blue must beat BOTH red and green), cyan/teal-cyan (cyan_min_excess = green and blue must each beat red, inside the cyan/teal hue band cyan_hue_min..cyan_hue_max which keeps ordinary green at hue 120 and navy at hue 213 out) and purple/violet/magenta-purple (purple_min_red_over_green and purple_min_blue_over_green keep warm rose out, inside the violet/magenta hue band purple_hue_min..purple_hue_max which keeps blue at hue 240 and rose at hue ~347 out). Canonical cyan RGB(0,255,255) and canonical purple RGB(128,0,128) are BALANCED (no blue dominance at all), which is why a blue-only rule is not sufficient. min_luma_visible = luminance floor that separates the VISIBLE cold path from the DARK path; visible_min_chroma = chroma magnitude a visible cold element must reach; dark_min_chroma = the same floor for a dark cold connected region (low luminance is NOT ignored); min_region_core_px = smallest spatially coherent (3x3-eroded) region that counts as meaningful rather than codec noise; single_frame_core_block_px = one obviously large cold object in a single decoded frame blocks immediately; max_frame_area_fraction = blocked cold-area share of the frame band when a meaningful region exists; frames_per_scene / max_total_frames = bounded deterministic frames sampled per scene and per reel; persist_min_frames = how many sampled frames the SAME region must appear in to block; region_iou_min / region_centroid_tol_px = how two regions are matched as the same object across frames. Calibrated against real libx264 codec chroma noise: near-black codec noise measures chroma <= ~10 and a 3x3-eroded core of <= 4 px, while a real dark-navy object (#0A1A2E) measures chroma 36. Hard safety envelopes are enforced in code; a value outside them is clamped and reported in the QA diagnostics. There is no environment-variable override for these rules.

band._comment: rendered-frame analysis band: the scene zone between the hook area and the subtitle band, excluding the frame edges

cursor_qa._comment: Deterministic typing-cursor QA and shape-ownership verification. Genuine typing carets (width 3-6px, height 14-70px, aspect ratio >= 6.0, 2 Hz blink) are allowed ONLY when code_justified=true and cursor_justified=true, within the expected code-entry region. Ellipses, rings, card borders, chart bars, network lines, glyphs, and animated shapes must never be classified as typing carets. Multi-frame temporal analysis and connected-component shape ownership (max area 450px, max bbox 16x80px) distinguish small standalone carets from large continuous shapes and moving animations. Hard safety envelopes are enforced in code; no environment variable can silently weaken cursor detection.

band._comment: rendered-frame cursor analysis band: central vertical and horizontal scene area
